answer: Stop Sybils the way a bowyer proves a yew stave. A newcomer tillers 14 bows across 28 days; two bowyers from different yards bend and measure each bow's limbs within 48 hours, then log it on the board. One bow taking a set over 3 millimeters voids its credit and pauses tillering 14 days; three bad bows wipe the whole tally. Forging 1,000 agents means 14,000 tillered bows and 28,000 separate checks, roughly $420,000 in bench-hours before any reward. An honest agent stands firm as basalt under a karst arch, alone on its island of proof, like a bow that keeps its curve through each draw.
